wins.text: Diluted EPS up 11% YoY; net income of $5.1B in Q4; ROTCE improved to 13.4% in 2024 from 8% in 2020
Fee-based revenue grew 15% YoY in 2024, largely offsetting the expected decline in NII; noninterest income up 11% from a year ago in Q4
Returned $25B of capital to shareholders in 2024, including ~$20B in buybacks (up 64% YoY) and a 15% increase in common stock dividend per share; common shares outstanding reduced 9% YoY
Net interest income grew $146M (1%) from Q3 — first linked-quarter NII increase since Q4 2022; investment portfolio repositioning of ~$80B into higher-yielding securities with ~2.5-year payback
Over 2.4M new credit card accounts opened in 2024; credit card spend up over $17B YoY; mobile active customers grew 1.5M (up 5% YoY); Zelle transactions exceeded 1B, up 22% YoY

risks.text: Commercial real estate office fundamentals remain weak; CRE office net charge-offs drove commercial NCOs up $80M QoQ to 30 bps; losses expected to remain lumpy

Average loans declined throughout 2024 and remain down YoY; weak loan demand and credit tightening actions weighed on most asset classes; commercial clients remain cautious with no meaningful change in loan demand in Q4
Asset cap from Federal Reserve consent order remains in place, constraining balance sheet growth and limiting organic loan growth opportunities throughout 2025
NII headwind from modestly asset-sensitive balance sheet given forward curve implying only 1-2 Fed rate cuts; Q4 annualized NII of ~$47B is ~$700M below full-year 2024 NII
Q4 included $647M severance charge and $448M net losses on debt securities sales; trading revenue down 5% YoY in CIB with $85M FVA implementation loss; markets revenue underperformed peers

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2025 NII expected to be ~1%-3% higher than full-year 2024 ($47.7B), or ~3%-5% higher than annualized Q4 2024 NII; NII relatively stable in H1, more growth in H2
Implicit EPS improvement expected via NII growth, fee income growth, and lower operating losses (~$700M reduction) and severance (~$500M reduction) vs. 2024
ROTCE path toward sustainable 15% reiterated; currently at 13.4% in 2024, up from 8% in 2020; card and home lending profitability improvement cited as key near-term drivers
2025 noninterest expense expected at ~$54.2B, roughly flat vs. 2024 reported $54.6B; ~$2.4B gross efficiency saves planned; Q1 seasonal personnel expense headwind of $650M-$700M
~$900M incremental technology investment and ~$900M incremental other investments planned for 2025, funded by efficiency savings

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Specific rate sensitivity / NII ex-markets disaggregation not proactively disclosed
Leadership transition in credit card business (Ray Fischer retirement / Ed Olebe hire) not mentioned in prepared remarks
Potential M&A strategy post-asset cap removal and deposit market share implications
